recipes.name: Spanish Moroccan Fish
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed
2 red bell peppers, seeded and sliced into strips

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in onion and garlic; cook and stir until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garbanzo beans, bell peppers, carrot, tomatoes, and olives; continue to cook until peppers are slightly tender, about 5 minutes more.

Sprinkle parsley, cumin, paprika, chicken bouillon, and cayenne over vegetables. Season with salt. Stir to incorporate. Place tilapia on top of vegetables and add enough water to cover vegetables. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until fish flakes easily with a fork and juices run clear, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spanish Moroccan Fish
raw_recipe.description: This Moroccan and Spanish fish recipe is made with garlic, onion, and a variety of spices that can be served either hot or cold, according to taste.

review.reviewBody: Very good! I changed the servings to two for the amounts of fish and veggies but changed the servings to 4 for the amount of spices to use. I also used both kalamata and spanish olives, I also used 1 cup olives. Not being a huge fan of beans, I replaced with broccoli. Spicy, great tasting. The fish just soaks up all that flavor. My husband was very suprised by this dish. He loved it.

Yes, sautéed onion quarters , garlic in two tablespoons butter and olive oil in cast iron skillet... add orange roughy cook on medium high four minutes added cumin, paprika, and parsley, cover for four minutes. In a second pot place whole green beans and cook in water and one tablespoon butter. Remove after boiled set aside. Next added garbanzos and diced tomato ring fish to the top of the vegetables and cover for another ten minutes. After strain green beans and place on shallow dish as a bed of beans add the veggies from the skillet and place the fish over veggies to drain juice over… made for two… so enjoy… better half says do it again…

My husband and I really liked this. I used thawed frozen cod fillets that I pressed some of the liquid out of using paper towels. I found this recipe in the magazine, and there is an editors suggestion to remove the fish after 15-16 min, then reduce the liquid in the sauce until it is as thick as you want it. I did that and ended up with a thick and yummy sauce. I served each fillet over a pine nut couscous from a box (Near East) and spooned the veggie mixture over that. I reduced the cayenne by more than 2/3 and it was plenty spicy for us. I also reduced the cumin a little. I have to say the result I got was much more appealing to look at than the photos would lead you to believe. I'm excited to make this again!

after reading the reviews it's very apparent you need to reduce the amount of fish and up the veggies.. i cut this down to 3 servings and used a little over a pound of tilapia.. i reduced the cayenne to 1/8 tsp and upped the bouillon to 4 tsp.. i used the following amounts for the veggies: 1/2 an onion, 3 cloves garlic, 1 red bell pepper, a large handful of baby carrots, 1 huge beefsteak tomato, a handful of olives, a little over a cup of kale, no garbanzos and cilantro for the parsley.. instead of cooking the fish on top i put it under the mixture.. i also didn't add water as there was enough liquid from the tomato.. about 10 minutes in i realized i forgot the olives so i added them and saw the fish was already done.. i wanted something more like a stew so i flaked the fish and stirred everything together.. i was going to make some kind of rice to serve it over but it already looked pretty hearty.. this tasted fine on it's own but i added chopped cilantro and a squirt of lemon over mine.. i don't think this will be a do over but it was fun to try something different

I followed the recipe, and it was incredible! I used kalamata and Spanish olives, chopped, and leftover chicken stock for the water. I used tomato on the vine variety, and they just melted away. Don't know if that was supposed to happen, but the end result was great! I was worried about simmering the fish for so long, but I just turned them a couple of times as they floated on top of the broth, then removed the lid for the last fifteen minutes or so to thicken the sauce. Served over Orso, because that's what I had. This was really good, and simple and so full of flavor! Will make again! Thank you so much!

YUM!!! I only used 3 pounds of tilapia with the veggie and spices remaining the same and it was good and made a HUGE portion. Also, I changed the cooking method because I wanted to put it in the oven and leave it alone: I put the vegetable/spices/chickpeas mixture in a 9 x 13 baking dish, rubbed both sides of the fillets with the mixture, placed them on top of the vegetables, poured about a cup of chicken broth instead of the bouillon/water mix and baked for 25 min or so at 375 degrees (temp suggested by another user as well). Served with rice and crusty bread.

I included potatoes and substituted green peppers for red. I also baked it as suggested by others which made the fish so tasty as it absorbed the sauce/spices. I also used additional spices from @TheSpiceHouse in Chicago: Vulcan Fire Salt and Moroccan Spice Mixture. It was delish!!!

Great recipe! Made it for company and they loved it. Of course, obligatory modifications: used caper berries instead of olives, 2 lbs of fresh halibut instead of tilapia, only used 3 tablespoons of cumin (same as paprika), used canned chopped tomatoes and chicken broth instead of water + bullion.

Absolutely an EXCELLENT recipe! My non-fish-loving husband gulfed this down in 5 minutes! I followed the recipe along with some of the raters' suggestions. These are the changes I made: 1) Cut down serving size for 2 for fish/veggies & serving for 4 for the spices (as another rater did) 2) used dry parsley since I didn't have fresh ones on hand 3) used 1 cup mixed black & green olives sliced 4) added 1 sliced serrano pepper to add more spice (we love spicy) 5) added 1/2 cup raisins to the dish. I also cooked the fish for 40 mins as the recipe said, but I think it would have been done in 30 mins (it started to break apart at 40 mins). 
I served the fish with the easy curry coucous (recipe found on this site) without the raisins in that recipe...the dishes combined was a GREAT hit!

I made this for 6, but used the full amounts of vegetables for 12 servings, and 6 tilapia fillets, which totaled slightly under 2 lb. But, the fish definitely does not need to cook for 40 minutes--10 to 15 was plenty. Good flavor and texture. I'll be doing this again.

My fiance and I loved this dish -- especially he did and he's not a big fish fan. I used what I had on hand which was about a pound of cod, so I cut the recipe down accordingly.

I also read reviews first and thus added more kick; I used Spanish smoked paprika. 

I also crumbled one dried small chili, one medium ancho chilli and cut up one dried chipotle chili. I also added one more olive. Wow! What kick! The smoky flavors of the paprika and the chipotle complemented everything and the flavor profile was awesome! This is definitely a "do it again"!
Tasty but way too salty. If I make it again I will substitute water for the chicken broth.
Followed the recipe and only adjusted the spices to my own personal taste. This recipe is a keeper for sure!

I made a half batch for my wife & I. From prep to eating just over an hour on a weeknight. I added a little too much chicken broth (substituted water) and it was more of a soup than the pictures of the dishes I saw. We both liked it a lot. This is one of those cooking mistakes that worked out for the better!
Only used two chicken breast and used Kentucky windage to determine the measure of ingredients.
If I make it again, I will season the fish after adding it to the pan. The vegetables had a nice flavor, but the fish was mild...too mild.
I have made this twice now, so good! I love how light it is, I added more olives, but that is just my taste.
